stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab to become very severe storm in 12 hours, make landfall on October 28
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab to become very severe storm in 12 hours, make landfall on October 28
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The IMD expects the storm to continue moving west-northwestwards while gaining strength over the next 12 hours.

New Delhi: Severe cyclonic storm Arnab, currently moving across the west-central Bay of Bengal, is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm within the next 12 hours before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned on Monday.

The weather department has issued a red-message cyclone warning for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining southern Odisha, forecasting powerful winds reaching 140 kmph, accompanied by heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several areas.

According to the IMD's latest bulletin, issued based on observations recorded at 5.30 pm on Monday, the cyclone is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, during the forenoon of October 28.
The storm is expected to make landfall with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115–125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph.

The cyclonic system, pronounced 'Ornab', moved west-northwestwards at a speed of 17 kmph during the six hours preceding the latest observation, strengthening into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal.
At 5.30 pm, the cyclone was centred near latitude 15.6°N and longitude 87.3°E, approximately 490 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 490 km south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha.
The system was also located around 560 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 660 km east of Machilipatnam and 730 km east of Bapatla.
It was positioned approximately 730 km northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman Islands.
It is forecast to maintain this trajectory until the evening of October 27 before gradually turning northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coastline.
If the projected track remains unchanged, the cyclone will cross the coast near Yanam on the morning of October 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm.
With the cyclone approaching the eastern coastline, the IMD has issued red and orange alerts for several districts of Odisha, warning of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.

stories.headline: Ajay Devgn wraps up Kargil shoot for ‘Chauhaan’
stories.title: Ajay Devgn wraps up Kargil shoot for ‘Chauhaan’
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 26: Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn has wrapped up the Kargil shooting schedule of his upcoming film Chauhaan. The actor returned to Kargil in Ladakh on October 14 after a gap of 23 years to shoot the film, revisiting the mountainous region where he had earlier filmed portions of the 2003 war drama LOC: Kargil. A member of the production team overseeing the shoot told Rising Kashmir that Devgn had completed the Kargil schedule and returned to Mumbai. “The actor has finished the Kargil shoot. He has flown back to Mumbai,” the team member said. On Saturday, Devgn was spotted at the hill station of Sonamarg. According to the production team member, the actor stayed there overnight after completing the shoot before leaving the following day via Srinagar. The film is directed by Neeraj Yadav and produced by Jyoti Deshpande, Aanand L Rai and Himanshu Sharma under Jio Studios and Colour Yellow Productions. The film is scheduled for theatrical release on October 1, 2027. The project was announced on June 25, 2026, the birth anniversary of Devgn’s late father, action director Veeru Devgan. Its promotional video introduced the actor in an intense action avatar and ended with the dialogue, “Pathaanon se kehna, Chauhaan aa raha hai” (Tell the Pathaans, Chauhaan is coming). Rising Kashmir learnt that the actor enjoyed Kargil’s cold weather, much like he did during an earlier shoot in the region in 2003. Devgn’s association with Jammu and Kashmir extends beyond his two visits to Ladakh for LOC: Kargil and Chauhaan. In 1999, he starred in Dil Kya Kare, directed by Prakash Jha and produced by his father, Veeru Devgan, alongside Veena Devgan and Kumaar Mangat. The film featured Kajol, Mahima Chaudhry and Chandrachur Singh and explored themes of love, family and difficult personal choices. In 2024, Devgn returned to Kashmir for Rohit Shetty’s Singham Again, the fifth instalment in the filmmaker’s popular cop universe. The film’s shooting schedule included sequences filmed in Srinagar’s downtown, Lal Chowk and Sonamarg in May 2024, with Devgn appearing alongside Jackie Shroff. The shoot drew attention from residents as the production team filmed action sequences under tight security.

stories.headline: Ather Energy posts first profit as EV demand outstrips supply
stories.title: Ather Energy posts first profit as EV demand outstrips supply
stories.summary: Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy reported its first profit in the September quarter, becoming the first major standalone EV company in India to turn a profit.Net income for the quarter was Rs 1.26 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 154 crore a year earlier. Its shares closed the day 14 percent higher on the NSE. The results were announced during market hours.Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Tarun Mehta, however, said the company isn't watching profit most closely.“PAT [profit after tax] is not the first thing to focus on,” Mehta said on an earnings call. The priority is the top line and volume, which bring operating leverage, he said.To enhance capacity, the board approved an expansion plan on Monday. Ather will add 2.25 lakh units of annual capacity, taking the total to about 11.4 lakh by the September quarter of fiscal 2028, compared with the 9.2 lakh units previously planned. It will invest about Rs 122 crore across its two sites: Hosur in Tamil Nadu and its new facility in Auric City in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Also Read: Ather Launches Konarc Scooter Starting at Rs99,999“If all the capacity work that we are putting in bears fruit well over the next few months, then I believe that PAT will take care of itself,” Mehta said, adding that profit “can go up and down” in the near term.Ather’s startup rival Ola Electric remains loss-making. Bigger rivals are better placed. Bajaj Auto’s EV business, spanning two- and three-wheelers, already runs at double-digit Ebitda margins. TVS Motor doesn’t report its EV profitability separately.EV sales have surged since the Iran war broke out in March and have continued. Ather said pre-orders more than doubled to 1.80 lakh in the quarter, while enquiries also rose 109 percent to about 10 lakh.Its Hosur plant ran at 98 percent utilisation at peak production, and Ather made about 33,000 vehicles a month on average, up from 28,000 in the June quarter. Mehta said the company is leaving roughly 20,000 units a month of retail demand unserved.With the approved expansion plan, Hosur capacity will rise by 75,000 units a year, from 4.2 lakh to 4.95 lakh, by December.The Auric plant will begin phased commercial production in December, with Phase 1 at 5 lakh units a year, or about 42,000 a month. Another 12,000 units a month, taking annual capacity to 6.5 lakh, is due by the September quarter of FY28.Also Read: TVS Motor to ramp up EV capacity by up to 25 percent by year-endMehta said trial production at Auric should begin in the coming weeks and installation will be complete by the March quarter.The base capacity will take about two quarters to ramp up fully.Even with both plants, he said, monthly capacity of 77,000 units would leave little headroom against current demand of 50,000-60,000 a month, which is why the expansion was brought forward.In the quarter gone by, Ather’s revenue rose 62 percent to Rs 1,527 crore, while wholesale volume rose 42 percent to 93,211 units. Revenue per vehicle was about Rs 1.57 lakh.It reported Ebitda of Rs 74.2 crore, a margin of 4.9 percent against a negative 9.6 percent a year earlier, an improvement of about 1,450 basis points. It was the second straight positive quarter, after a margin of 0.8 percent in the June quarter.The average ex-showroom price rose to about Rs 1,64,000 from about Rs 1,50,000 in the March quarter. Ather attributed that to price increases and a richer product mix.Its non-vehicle revenue rose to 15 percent of revenue from operations from 12 percent a year earlier. Some 94 percent of buyers took the AtherStack Pro software pack. More than half of non-vehicle revenue comes from that pack, which Mehta said carries gross margins of 80-90 percent.Also Read: How Ather’s foray into mass market pits it against giant incumbents TVS, BajajCommodity pressureAdjusted gross margin was 24 percent, up 160 basis points from a year earlier, though below the 25.4 percent of the March quarter.Aluminium, copper, lithium and plastics stayed expensive through the quarter. Mehta said hopes of relief earlier this year, tied to a resolution of the Hormuz crisis, proved wrong. He said aluminium has shown some signs of cooling in recent days.“We are not out of the woods,” Mehta said. He called the commodity squeeze temporary but said it has lasted “a few quarters longer” than he expected.Ather doesn’t plan more price increases in the December quarter, he said, and commodity costs look broadly flat for now.Industry registrations rose 82 percent to about 5.98 lakh units, and electric penetration of scooter sales reached 11.2 percent for the quarter, up from 7.8 percent. It hit a record 11.6 percent in September.Ather’s own registrations, including exports, rose about 60 percent to 92,500 units, trailing the industry. Its market share slipped to 15.1 percent from 17.2 percent a year earlier.The Bengaluru-based company launched its new mass-market e-scooter, the Konarc, on August 29. Built on a new platform, the company says the scooter is aimed at petrol buyers.Fewer than 10,000 Konarcs were sold in September, and only in a few northern markets.Mehta said enquiries, pre-orders and walk-ins there were “up several times”. He said the early reaction was that it is “finally a proper scooter, and not just an electric one.”

opening: Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy reported its first profit in the September quarter, becoming the first major standalone EV company in India to turn a profit.
Net income for the quarter was Rs 1.26 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 154 crore a year earlier.
body: Its shares closed the day 14 percent higher on the NSE.
The results were announced during market hours.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Tarun Mehta, however, said the company isn't watching profit most closely.
“PAT [profit after tax] is not the first thing to focus on,” Mehta said on an earnings call.
The priority is the top line and volume, which bring operating leverage, he said.
To enhance capacity, the board approved an expansion plan on Monday.
Ather will add 2.25 lakh units of annual capacity, taking the total to about 11.4 lakh by the September quarter of fiscal 2028, compared with the 9.2 lakh units previously planned.
It will invest about Rs 122 crore across its two sites: Hosur in Tamil Nadu and its new facility in Auric City in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

“If all the capacity work that we are putting in bears fruit well over the next few months, then I believe that PAT will take care of itself,” Mehta said, adding that profit “can go up and down” in the near term.
Ather’s startup rival Ola Electric remains loss-making.
Bigger rivals are better placed.
Bajaj Auto’s EV business, spanning two- and three-wheelers, already runs at double-digit Ebitda margins.
TVS Motor doesn’t report its EV profitability separately.
EV sales have surged since the Iran war broke out in March and have continued.
Ather said pre-orders more than doubled to 1.80 lakh in the quarter, while enquiries also rose 109 percent to about 10 lakh.
Mehta said the company is leaving roughly 20,000 units a month of retail demand unserved.
With the approved expansion plan, Hosur capacity will rise by 75,000 units a year, from 4.2 lakh to 4.95 lakh, by December.
The Auric plant will begin phased commercial production in December, with Phase 1 at 5 lakh units a year, or about 42,000 a month.
Another 12,000 units a month, taking annual capacity to 6.5 lakh, is due by the September quarter of FY28.
Mehta said trial production at Auric should begin in the coming weeks and installation will be complete by the March quarter.
The base capacity will take about two quarters to ramp up fully.
Even with both plants, he said, monthly capacity of 77,000 units would leave little headroom against current demand of 50,000-60,000 a month, which is why the expansion was brought forward.
Revenue per vehicle was about Rs 1.57 lakh.
It reported Ebitda of Rs 74.2 crore, a margin of 4.9 percent against a negative 9.6 percent a year earlier, an improvement of about 1,450 basis points.
The average ex-showroom price rose to about Rs 1,64,000 from about Rs 1,50,000 in the March quarter.
Ather attributed that to price increases and a richer product mix.
Some 94 percent of buyers took the AtherStack Pro software pack.
Aluminium, copper, lithium and plastics stayed expensive through the quarter.
Mehta said hopes of relief earlier this year, tied to a resolution of the Hormuz crisis, proved wrong.
He said aluminium has shown some signs of cooling in recent days.
“We are not out of the woods,” Mehta said.
He called the commodity squeeze temporary but said it has lasted “a few quarters longer” than he expected.
Ather doesn’t plan more price increases in the December quarter, he said, and commodity costs look broadly flat for now.
It hit a record 11.6 percent in September.
The Bengaluru-based company launched its new mass-market e-scooter, the Konarc, on August 29.
Built on a new platform, the company says the scooter is aimed at petrol buyers.
Fewer than 10,000 Konarcs were sold in September, and only in a few northern markets.
Mehta said enquiries, pre-orders and walk-ins there were “up several times”.
He said the early reaction was that it is “finally a proper scooter, and not just an electric one.”

stories.headline: Media association challenges privacy law in Supreme Court
stories.title: Media association challenges privacy law in Supreme Court
stories.summary: A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is scheduled to hear a batch of petitions filed by activists on October 27
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
event term: 'chief justice of india' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), which has members drawn from across the media spectrum, including those owned by the Ambani and Adani Groups, have challenged the Union government’s privacy law as a violation of journalistic freedom.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is scheduled to hear a batch of petitions filed by activists on October 27.

The petition filed by the DNPA, which is also listed before the Bench, challenged specific provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025.
The DNPA said the law was completely in contravention with the law laid down by the Supreme Court in its privacy judgment, which held the right inviolable and fundamental to human dignity and life.
“They impermissibly restrict the fundamental right to information and freedom of speech and expression,” the petition said.

The law fails “to provide any exemption in favour of journalistic activity as a distinct class of processing, entitled to constitutional protection under Article 14 and 19(l)(a) of the Constitution of India and threatens the full spectrum of Journalistic activity carried out by journalists, ground reporters, citizens, whistleblowers, RTI activists, and other stakeholders, and strikes at the core of our democratic framework and runs contrary to the basic tenets of the Constitution of India,” the petition said.
It said publishers, editors, reporters and correspondents were, as a consequence of the law, brought within a regime of notice and prior consent, compelled erasure, and verifiable consent.

Section 36 of the DPDP Act, read with Rule 23 and the Seventh Schedule of the DPDP Rules, vested the Central government with an unbridled and standardless authority to requisition any information from any data fiduciary or intermediary, unaccompanied by judicial oversight, any requirement of necessity or proportionality, or notice to the affected data principal.
“Such a power is capable of being turned to the identification and targeting of journalistic sources and is thus constitutionally infirm,” the petition said.
Section 44 (3) of the DPDP Act, by amending Section 8 (1 )(j) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, has placed every category of “personal information” beyond the reach of disclosure.
Further, by amending the Right to Information Act 2005, the DPDP Act has created an absolute bar on the seeking of information relating to public offices.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the elevation of four High Court judges as Chief Justices of various High Courts.
As per the Collegium's statement issued today, Justice P Sam Koshy, currently serving at the Telangana High Court, has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court.
The Collegium has also recommended Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak of the Gujarat High Court for appointment as Chief Justice of the same High Court.
Further, Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty, currently serving at the Calcutta High Court, has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court.
Justice Sudhir Singh of the Patna High Court has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court.
The recommendations were announced through a statement issued by the Supreme Court Collegium following its meeting on October 26.

stories.headline: Tata Motors completes Iveco acquisition to turbocharge global play
stories.title: Tata Motors completes Iveco acquisition to turbocharge global play
stories.summary: The $4.5 billion deal will expand the Indian automaker’s global footprint and strengthens its presence across commercial vehicle segments.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Tata Motors Ltd has completed the acquisition of Italian truckmaker Iveco Group, marking a major step in the Indian commercial vehicle giant’s expansion into global markets and new product segments.
The deal comes after a 15-month process that faced delays and resistance from some minority shareholders over the offer price.

An update on the Italian stock exchange late on Monday, showed that the transaction had been completed after the tender offer for Iveco shares closed with nearly 88% of the shares tendered, paving the way for the integration of the two commercial vehicle businesses.
The acquisition, first announced in July 2025, has an enterprise value of about $4.5 billion.
The increase in tendering on Monday suggested that Tata Motors had won over most shareholders who had not voted at the extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on 16 October.
About 12% of shareholders voted against resolutions related to the deal, while 35% did not vote.
About 53% voted in favour.

Tata Sons' chairperson Natarajan Chandrasekaran, Jaguar Land Rover's chief executive P.B. Balaji, and Tata Motors' managing director Girish Wagh are among the top executives set to join Iveco’s board.

The deal—initially expected to close by June but delayed owing to regulatory approvals—brings together two commercial vehicle makers with a combined annual sales volume of more than 540,000 vehicles and revenue of over $25 billion.
The combined business will have a much wider geographic footprint, with Europe accounting for about half of sales, India 35% and the Americas the remaining 15%, as per its earlier disclosures.
Tata Motors had earlier noted that the acquisition will help it gain access to geographies and segments where its commercial vehicle business has had a limited presence.
Iveco has a strong position in Europe and is the third largest commercial vehicle maker in Latin America, while Tata Motors has a more established presence in India and parts of Africa.

An update on the Italian stock exchange late on Monday, showed that the transaction had been completed after the tender offer for Iveco shares closed with nearly 88% of the shares tendered, paving the way for the integration of the two commercial vehicle businesses.
The increase in tendering on Monday suggested that Tata Motors had won over most shareholders who had not voted at the extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on 16 October.
